speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you tell me the gestational age at birth and if there was any meconium staining in the amniotic fluid? Also, did the baby require immediate resuscitation or intubation right after delivery?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, born at 33 weeks of gestation. The newborn is presenting with respiratory distress 2 hours after birth. The mother had an uneventful pregnancy until premature onset of labor. There was no significant prenatal care history mentioned.

speaker: Doctor
text: Was there a history of maternal fever, chorioamnionitis, or prolonged rupture of membranes prior to delivery? Additionally, did the mother receive any antenatal corticosteroids to promote fetal lung maturity?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Respiratory distress. I also have Grunting, Intercoastal and subcostal retractions, Peripheral cyanosis.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray

The X-ray will help us distinguish between respiratory distress syndrome and other causes like pneumonia or pneumothorax given the prematurity and symptoms. Please describe the radiographic findings once the results are available.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Chest Radiograph: Fine reticular granulation with ground glass appearance on both lungs.

speaker: Doctor
text: The chest X-ray findings of a ground-glass appearance with reticular granulation are classic for Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS) in a premature infant. Given the gestational age of 33 weeks and the lack of maternal infection signs, this clinical picture is highly consistent with surfactant deficiency. DIAGNOSIS READY: Neonatal Respiratory Distress Syndrome
